acceptance_criteria: In the hosted chat (chat.html), after a substantive answered turn that used advisor tools (e.g. a transitions comparison), between 2 and 4 clickable follow-up prompt chips appear below the reply, and clicking one sends that chip's text as the user's next chat message without retyping.

Follow-up prompts are drawn only from a fixed static allowlist whose entries map 1:1 onto the twelve shipped advisor tools; an automated allowlist-membership test fails if the derivation can emit any string outside that allowlist or if an allowlist entry references a tool not registered in tool_dispatch.
A turn that ends in an error reply, the fallback reply, or a rate-limited response shows no follow-up chips, and the chat surface still renders and accepts input normally.
The assistant's reply prose is unchanged by this feature: no menu phrasing is added to reply text, and the existing handback-guard and chat tests stay green.

Headless-Chromium E2E evidence via pytest-playwright on the CI ubuntu runner shows the chips render after a stubbed answered turn, a chip click round-trips as a new user message, and the page produces zero page-generated console errors and zero failed page requests (a failed request fails the test naming the failed URL, including /favicon.ico), with no live provider call and no OPENROUTER_API_KEY present.
The full applicable automated test suite (pytest -q, the repository's canonical test command run by .github/workflows/tests.yml) passes on the merged result.

operating_envelope.requirement: A representative heavy turn whose tool calls span many of the twelve advisor tools still yields at most 4 follow-up prompts, keeping the chip row bounded on desktop and mobile widths.
operating_envelope.failure_condition: Any derivation input produces 5 or more follow-up prompts.

operating_envelope.requirement: When a turn has no successful tool results (error-only turn, no-tool turn, or the fallback reply), follow-up derivation returns an empty list so the client renders no chips and degrades to today's behavior.
operating_envelope.failure_condition: An error-only or no-tool turn yields a non-empty follow-up list.

operating_envelope.requirement: Follow-up prompts arrive inline in the same /api/chat JSON response that carries the reply; rendering them requires no additional endpoint or network round trip.
operating_envelope.failure_condition: The client must issue any HTTP request beyond the existing single /api/chat POST to obtain or render follow-ups.

operating_envelope.requirement: The browser E2E suite runs against a locally served webapp with a stubbed chat backend, with OPENROUTER_API_KEY unset, and issues no request to any live model or government-data provider.
operating_envelope.failure_condition: The E2E suite fails without a live API key, or any request during the E2E run targets a non-localhost host.

adr.title: Deterministic allowlist-derived follow-up prompts, shared across both chat backends, with pytest-playwright browser assurance
adr.context: Issue #37 asks for contextual, clickable follow-up prompts after a useful answer, drawn only from capabilities the product actually supports, preserving 'answer first, then reveal relevant supported capabilities' (CAREER_ADVISOR_PROTOCOL.md rule 11 already forbids operator-style menus in reply prose). product.md standing constraint 5 forbids implying unsupported capabilities. The repository has two chat backends (chat.py OpenRouter tool-loop and chat_cli.py) that both return ChatReply and already share per-turn tool-result extraction via chat_extract.extract_candidates_and_plan; the frontend already renders server-supplied clickable choices (renderCandidates in static/chat.js) that disable when stale. Prompt-only behavioral fixes have historically regressed and required code guards (issues #52 handback_guard, #60 current_occupation_guard). There is no browser-test tooling in requirements-dev.txt or .github/workflows/tests.yml, no favicon in static/, and the webapp is a free-tier, no-persistence surface. Project #64 requires browser/E2E evidence for any hosted-chat change.
adr.decision: Derive follow-ups deterministically on the server, not from the model: a new small module (career_intelligence_mcp/followups.py) maps the turn's tool-call results plus established session state onto 0-4 prompt strings taken from a static literal allowlist whose entries map 1:1 onto the twelve tools registered in tool_dispatch, so no string outside the allowlist can ever be emitted. Both backends surface it through a new ChatReply.followups field populated alongside the existing shared chat_extract call; webapp.py passes it through as ChatResponse.followups in the same /api/chat response; static/chat.js renders it as clickable chips below the reply, reusing the candidate-picker pattern (click sends the text; stale chips disable). Reply prose is untouched. Add explicit /favicon.ico handling (a successful response) to the webapp surface. Browser assurance uses route 2 of the planning contract: authorize the established pytest-playwright dependency (headless Chromium, CI's ubuntu-latest runner, browser install as its own CI step), running the webapp locally with a stubbed chat backend, capturing page console errors and failed page requests. Story issues live in the product repository (product stories belong with product code); the factory merge gate for this private repository is only the existing Tests workflow required check — no cross-repository factory gate exists and none is claimed.
alternatives: Model-generated follow-up suggestions (ask the LLM to propose next prompts): rejected — it can invent unsupported capabilities, violating product.md constraint 5, and prompt-only behavior has demonstrably regressed before (issues #52/#60 needed code guards).

Prompt-only change instructing the model to append a menu of options to its reply text: rejected — CAREER_ADVISOR_PROTOCOL.md rule 11 explicitly forbids operator-style menus in prose, and it is untestable deterministically.
A homemade browser driver (raw Chromium process, CDP, --dump-dom): rejected — the planning contract forbids invented drivers, and no such mechanism exists in this repository.
Skipping browser evidence and relying on TestClient-level tests only: rejected — Project #64's finish line and product.md both require browser/E2E evidence for hosted-chat changes.
Placing generated planning artifacts in the factory repository: rejected — product stories belong with product code; the trigger and this plan keep them in career-intelligence-mcp.
consequences: Positive: unsupported capabilities structurally cannot appear as follow-ups — output is a subset of a reviewed static allowlist, enforced by tests asserting allowlist membership and allowlist-to-tool mapping.
Positive: both chat backends get identical follow-up behavior through the existing shared extraction seam, with no new subsystem, persistence, or protocol.
Positive: the repository gains its first reusable headless-browser E2E harness, plus favicon/failed-request assurance for the hosted chat.
Negative: a new dev dependency (pytest-playwright) and a browser-install CI step add roughly 1-2 minutes to CI runs.
Negative: deterministic chips are less context-sensitive than model-chosen suggestions; wording comes from a fixed allowlist the owner should eyeball at acceptance.
Negative: adding a future advisor tool requires updating the allowlist; the allowlist-to-dispatch mapping test turns a forgotten update into a visible failure rather than silent drift.

stories.title: Deterministic follow-up derivation shared by both chat backends
stories.spec: Add career_intelligence_mcp/followups.py: a pure function that takes the turn's ordered (tool_name, result_dict) pairs (the same list chat_extract.extract_candidates_and_plan consumes) plus the session's established_current_occupation, and returns 0-4 follow-up prompt strings selected from a static literal allowlist. Each allowlist entry is a plain-language prompt (no O*NET/SOC/endpoint terminology, per product.md) mapped 1:1 to one of the twelve tools registered in tool_dispatch (e.g. after find_career_transitions: certifications, training options, licenses, full transition plan; after build_career_transition_plan: job centers, employing industries). Suppress suggestions for capabilities already exercised this turn, and return [] for error-only turns, no-tool turns, and the fallback reply. Add ChatReply.followups (Optional[list], default None) in chat.py; populate it in chat.py's send_message next to the existing chat_extract call, and in chat_cli.py's send_message via the same shared derivation, so both backends behave identically. Reply prose is never modified. Proof obligation for the supported-only claim — Claim: every emitted follow-up names a shipped capability. Domain: all reachable outputs of the derivation function for any input. Invariant: outputs are selected by membership from a static literal allowlist; there is no dynamic string construction path. Skipped-value justification: since output is a subset of the allowlist, inputs not directly tested cannot produce a string outside it. Bound: allowlist size is at most 12 entries (one per registered tool), reviewed exhaustively by test. Falsification: a test asserting every allowlist entry's mapped tool name is in tool_dispatch's registered tool set, and a fuzz-style test asserting derivation output is a subset of the allowlist for varied inputs. Acceptance-to-scope mapping: career_intelligence_mcp/followups.py owns the derivation behavior; chat.py and chat_cli.py own the ChatReply plumbing; tests/test_followups.py (new) proves derivation properties; tests/test_chat.py and tests/test_chat_cli.py (existing files, new cases) prove backend wiring.

digest:
## Plan in plain language

After the Career Advisor gives a real answer, the chat page will show a small row of 2 to 4 clickable suggestion buttons under the reply — things like checking certifications, training options, or building a full transition plan. Clicking one sends that question for you, so you never have to guess what the advisor can do next. The suggestions are picked by simple server code from a fixed, reviewed list that matches exactly what the product already supports today — the AI model does not invent them, so it can never advertise something the product cannot do. The advisor's answer text itself does not change, and when a turn fails or is rate-limited, no suggestions appear. The plan also adds a proper favicon response and, for proof, a real headless-browser test (using the established Playwright tool in CI) that loads the chat page, sees the buttons, clicks one, and checks that the page produced no console errors and no failed requests. Two human decisions are expected: approving this plan, and accepting the finished outcome. One choice for the owner to watch at acceptance: the exact wording of the suggestion buttons.

## How the plan works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User message] --> A[/api/chat/]
  A --> B[chat backend tool loop]
  B --> T[Advisor tool results]
  T --> D[followups.py: deterministic allowlist derivation]
  D --> R[ChatReply.followups]
  R --> A2[/api/chat JSON response/]
  A2 --> C[chat.js renders clickable chips]
  C -->|chip click| U
```

In text: a user message hits /api/chat; the chat backend runs its normal tool loop; the turn's tool results feed a new deterministic derivation module (followups.py) that selects 0-4 prompts from a static allowlist mapped 1:1 to the twelve shipped tools; the prompts ride back inline on the same /api/chat response; chat.js renders them as clickable chips; clicking a chip sends its text as the next user message. Both backends (chat.py and chat_cli.py) use the same derivation. Error, fallback, and rate-limited turns carry no follow-ups.

## Story dependencies

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  followup-derivation --> chat-ui-followups --> browser-e2e-followups
```

In text: `followup-derivation` (build) has no dependencies and creates the shared deterministic derivation plus ChatReply plumbing in both backends. `chat-ui-followups` (build) depends on `followup-derivation` and adds the /api/chat passthrough, favicon handling, and the chip UI. `browser-e2e-followups` (ship, hazard: touches requirements-dev.txt and the CI workflow) depends on `chat-ui-followups` and adds pytest-playwright plus the headless-Chromium E2E that proves chips render, a click round-trips, and the page has zero console errors and zero failed requests including /favicon.ico, all without a live provider key. Unresolved choices surfaced, not decided silently: chip copy is owner-reviewable at acceptance; the operational-learning record for run #64 lives factory-side (factory/learning/ pattern), not as a product Story; and this repository's merge gate remains its Tests required check only — no cross-repository factory gate exists.
